customManagers.description: Track self-hosted (vendored) front-end assets via static/vendor/versions.txt; a PR here is a heads-up to re-vendor the dist files.

Track the explicitly pinned Alpine apk packages in the Dockerfile (each `ARG <PKG>_VERSION=x.y.z-rN` preceded by a `# renovate:` line) via repology, so every OS-package bump is a Renovate PR instead of silent drift.

Track the Chrome-for-Testing build the e2e leg pins (agent-browser fetches latest by default, which let Chrome 151 destabilize the 2-core leg — see #947). A bump is a Renovate PR that re-runs the e2e leg, so a new Chrome is verified green before it lands.

Track the pinned Shawl (Windows service wrapper) release in deps.py via github-releases (#934). Renovate bumps the `_*_VERSION` constant; the download URL derives from it in code, so version and URL can't drift. The `sha256` is NOT auto-updated (the hosted App reads github-releases' git-tag digest, not the release ASSET's file checksum), so refresh it from GitHub's published asset digest — `scripts/check_binary_dep_pins.py` verifies each pin against that digest and prints the correct value, and `deps install` fail-closes on a mismatch.

Track the Alpine image the `pytest on alpine musl` smoke-test in ci.yml runs via `docker run`. It duplicates the Dockerfile's `FROM alpine:` pin but lives in a workflow run-script (hoisted to the ALPINE_MUSL_IMAGE step env so this annotation sits on a mapping key), so neither the dockerfile nor github-actions manager sees it — this keeps the canary in lockstep with the shipped base. datasource/depName/versioning come from the annotation; currentDigest re-pins the sha alongside the version.

Track the BuildKit engine image pinned by DIGEST in docker/setup-buildx-action's `driver-opts` (release.yml + nightly.yml). Renovate's built-in github-actions manager already tracks the SIBLING buildx `version:` input on the same action, but it does NOT parse `driver-opts` — so without this the BuildKit half would drift silently while buildx got PRs. Both are pinned for #1189's digest-prediction reproducibility (the imagetools `--dry-run` must reproduce the published index digest) and must move deliberately together — held for review (see packageRules). versioning comes from the annotation; currentDigest re-pins the sha alongside the version.

Track the pinned actionlint (workflow linter) release in actionlint.yml via github-releases (#1170). Renovate bumps ONLY `ACTIONLINT_VERSION`; the download URL derives from it in the run-script, so version + URL can't drift. The adjacent `ACTIONLINT_SHA256` is NOT auto-updated (the hosted App reads github-releases' git-tag digest, not the release ASSET's tarball checksum), so a bump PR carries a stale hash until it is refreshed from the release's checksums.txt — the actionlint job's own `sha256sum -c` then fails loudly on the mismatch, so a stale hash can never silently ship. Held for review (see packageRules).

packageRules.description: atheris is pinned per-interpreter by hand in pyproject.toml — its wheel coverage shifts per release (3.1.0 dropped the cp311 wheel), so an auto-bump re-breaks the Python 3.11 CI leg (see #464 / #466). Renovate must not touch it. Remove this rule once Python 3.11 is dropped from the support matrix.

Do NOT float `.python-version`. It pins the CANONICAL dev interpreter (3.13 — the frozen binary + lint/build/coverage jobs all pin 3.13); it is not a dependency to bump. Renovate's `pyenv` manager (which tracks `.python-version`) bumping it to the newest CPython (#941: 3.13->3.14) silently overrode uv's interpreter — `uv run` in the lint job rebuilt the venv on 3.14 WITHOUT the dev extra, so ruff went missing and lint failed. Bump the canonical interpreter by hand, deliberately, like the CI matrix. (NB: the manager is `pyenv`, not `python-version` — the latter is a datasource, not a manager.)

js-yaml is pinned to v4 via an npm `overrides` entry in package.json — it is a transitive dep of markdownlint-cli2 (the dev-only `lint:md` tool), which does a default `import yaml from "js-yaml"`. js-yaml v5 is ESM-only and dropped the default export, so forcing v5 through the override breaks the required `lint` check (see #516). Cap Renovate below v5 until markdownlint-cli2 ships js-yaml v5 support; revisit then.
Vendored front-end assets require a manual dist re-vendor — never auto-merge; label for review.

Never auto-merge a hand-pinned binary-dep bump: Shawl, the Windows service wrapper (#934), or the claustrum Direct Session daemon (schubydoo/claustrum). Renovate updates the version + derived URL but CANNOT recompute the source-pinned sha256s. Self-hosted Renovate CE refreshes them in-branch via the postUpgradeTask (check_binary_dep_pins.py --fix rewrites every stale pin in deps.py from GitHub's published asset digests), so the bump + refreshed hashes land in one commit and the binary-dep-pins check passes. Still no auto-merge: a human eyeballs the refreshed pins before they ship (and if CE is down the task can't run, so the stale hash must be caught here). The command must be on RENOVATE_ALLOWED_POST_UPGRADE_COMMANDS.

Never auto-merge a BuildKit engine bump (moby/buildkit driver-opts). It is pinned for #1189's digest-prediction reproducibility, and its build steps (release.yml / nightly.yml) run only on release/nightly triggers — NOT on the Renovate PR — so nothing on the PR proves the new engine still produces a matching predicted digest. A maintainer bumps the buildx `version:` in lockstep and re-validates the prediction before shipping.

Never auto-merge an actionlint bump: Renovate updates ACTIONLINT_VERSION but CANNOT recompute the adjacent ACTIONLINT_SHA256 (the release's checksums.txt asset digest, not the git-tag digest the hosted App sees). A maintainer refreshes the hash from checksums.txt; until then the actionlint job's `sha256sum -c` fails and blocks the merge — fail-loud, never silent.
Auto-merge patch + minor updates of dev/test tooling once CI passes (a failing check blocks the merge).

Auto-merge the Dockerfile's pinned Alpine apk packages (repology). The pinned-apk model 404s a build the moment Alpine publishes a newer -rN, so bumps must flow promptly rather than wait on a manual merge; the docker smoke-test + musl smoke-test in CI gate them, and a failing check blocks the merge. Grouped into one PR to keep the noise down. Scoped to the Dockerfile so a future repology-sourced dep elsewhere doesn't inherit blanket auto-merge.

Hold mkdocs-redirects at 1.2.2 — the last release published from the mkdocs GitHub org. 1.2.3 moved the project to a third-party org and added a hard dependency on `properdocs`, a second documentation engine that lands in the docs environment and prints promotional output into every build; it also caps `mkdocs<=1.6.1`, which would block future MkDocs upgrades. pyproject pins `==1.2.2`; this upper bound is what stops Renovate re-proposing the bump (it opened #997 before this rule existed). Revisit if upstream publishes a release without the `properdocs` dependency, or when the docs site migrates off MkDocs (#996). Security advisories are unaffected — vulnerabilityAlerts bypasses allowedVersions.

Hold Alpine base-image MINOR bumps (e.g. 3.24 -> 3.25) for manual review: a minor can move the system python3 to a new interpreter minor the CI support matrix must move with, so it must not auto-merge on a green smoke-test alone. Patch bumps (3.24.x) and digest re-pins still auto-merge via the base policy — only minor is held. Covers both the Dockerfile FROM and the ci.yml musl canary (custom.regex) so the grouped bump below holds as one on a minor. Restores the pre-centralization clauster behavior (the old inline rule auto-merged Alpine patch only).

Lockstep the Alpine base image: the Dockerfile `FROM alpine:` and the ci.yml musl canary (ALPINE_MUSL_IMAGE) are the SAME image and must never diverge, so group every update type into ONE PR. This overrides the base `docker (non-major)` grouping for alpine only.

The ci.yml alpine canary is a custom.regex dep, which the base policy holds (automerge:false + `vendored` label). Restore the Dockerfile's automerge for it — patch + digest re-pins auto-merge on green CI (the musl smoke-test that runs this very image gates it) — so the grouped alpine-base PR merges hands-off, with no held follow-up to reconcile. Minor stays held by the rule above. Mirrors the existing repology-apk auto-merge precedent in this file. (The grouped PR still carries the `vendored` label the base adds to the custom.regex half — cosmetic.)

The browser-e2e tooling lockfile (tests/e2e/package.json: agent-browser + @puppeteer/browsers). Renovate's stock ignorePaths carried `**/tests/**`, which hid this file from every manager, so agent-browser sat at 0.27.1 from 2026-06 to 2026-08 while newer releases ran the suite 2.5-4 min faster; that ignore is dropped above (these two files are the only version-bearing ones under tests/). Never auto-merge: the e2e leg is a NON-required check, so a bump must be merged by a human who reads the run's rerun (`R`) marks, not the check colour. Each CLI bump stays its own PR (no group) so it gets its own e2e verdict — the base `npm (non-major)` group would otherwise fold it in once it leaves 0.x. The suite's driver carries the two guards a newer CLI needs (clauster PR 1270 lineage: click_run waits for the launch popover to close; goto retries the daemon-startup race on the session's first command). Last on purpose: later rules win per field.
